subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids and polymers

questions.q: What flame colour is produced by potassium ions in a flame test?
questions.explain: Potassium ions (K+) give a characteristic lilac flame colour.

questions.q: When sodium hydroxide solution is added to a solution of copper(II) ions, what colour is the precipitate formed?
questions.explain: Copper(II) ions form a blue precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide with sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: Which metal ion produces an orange-red (brick red) colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Calcium ions (Ca2+) give an orange-red flame colour.

questions.q: A solution gives a brown precipitate when sodium hydroxide is added. Which ion is present?
questions.explain: Iron(III) ions form a brown precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide with sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: Which metal ion forms a white precipitate with sodium hydroxide that then redissolves in excess sodium hydroxide?
questions.explain: Aluminium hydroxide is white but dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide, unlike calcium hydroxide which does not.

questions.q: Which procedure is the correct test for sulfate ions?
options: Add dilute hydrochloric acid, then barium chloride solution; a white precipitate forms
Add dilute nitric acid, then silver nitrate solution; a white precipitate forms
Add sodium hydroxide and warm; a gas turns damp red litmus blue
Add dilute acid; the gas turns limewater milky
questions.explain: Sulfate ions give a white precipitate of barium sulfate with acidified barium chloride solution.

questions.q: A solution is acidified with dilute nitric acid and silver nitrate solution is added, giving a cream precipitate. Which ion is present?
questions.explain: Bromide ions give a cream silver bromide precipitate, between the white (chloride) and yellow (iodide) results.

questions.q: Ammonium ions are tested by warming with sodium hydroxide solution. What is the positive result?
options: A gas is produced that turns damp red litmus paper blue
A white precipitate forms that dissolves in excess
A gas is produced that turns limewater milky
questions.explain: Ammonium ions release ammonia gas when warmed with alkali, and ammonia turns damp red litmus paper blue.

questions.q: What is the approximate size range of nanoparticles?
questions.explain: Nanoparticles range from roughly 1 to 100 nm in diameter, containing only a few hundred atoms.

questions.q: How does the surface area to volume ratio of a particle change as the particle gets smaller?
questions.explain: As particle size decreases, the surface area to volume ratio increases, which is why nanoparticles are so reactive.

questions.q: If the length of the side of a cube is decreased by a factor of 10, how does its surface area to volume ratio change?
options: It increases by a factor of 10
It decreases by a factor of 10
It increases by a factor of 100
questions.explain: For a cube, the surface area to volume ratio is inversely proportional to the side length, so dividing the side by 10 multiplies the ratio by 10.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common use of nanoparticles?
options: In sun creams to absorb and reflect UV light
As a fuel in car engines
As a structural metal in bridges
questions.explain: Nanoparticles are used in sun creams, and also as catalysts and in cosmetics, owing to their large surface area to volume ratio.

questions.q: What is the general formula for the alkanes?
questions.explain: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2, for example methane CH4 and ethane C2H6.

questions.q: What is the general formula for the alkenes?
questions.explain: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing a C=C double bond, with the general formula CnH2n.

questions.q: What colour change occurs when an alkene is shaken with bromine water?
questions.explain: Alkenes decolourise bromine water, turning it from orange to colourless, because the C=C double bond reacts with the bromine.

questions.q: What is the functional group of the carboxylic acids?
questions.explain: Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH functional group, for example ethanoic acid CH3COOH.

questions.q: What is the functional group of the alcohols?
questions.explain: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl -OH functional group, for example ethanol C2H5OH.

questions.q: Ethanol can be produced industrially by fermentation. Which of the following is needed for fermentation of sugars?
questions.explain: Fermentation uses yeast to convert sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide in the absence of oxygen.

questions.q: A carboxylic acid has two carbon atoms. What is its molecular formula?
questions.explain: Ethanoic acid has two carbon atoms and the formula CH3COOH (C2H4O2).

questions.q: In the addition polymerisation of ethene to form poly(ethene), what other product is formed?
questions.explain: In addition polymerisation the alkene monomers join together and the polymer is the only product, unlike condensation polymerisation which also releases a small molecule such as water.
